subject: Skyline Labs — MTAP & regional burst policy decisions
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MTAP draft + regional burst question

Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the deep dive yesterday. As promised I'm attaching an updated MTAP (skyline-mtap-v2.pdf) that captures the milestones we discussed: provisioning window, networking checklist, prewarm schedule, and the go/no-go criteria for the first three weeks of traffic. High level asks from our side:

- Confirm target peak sustained QPS and expected p50/p95 latency goals for text generation endpoints (you mentioned 350 qps during the demo).
- Confirm which clouds/regions you need primary vs failover (you said us-west-2 primary, eu-west-1 for DR).
- Procurement contact for reserved capacity contract and billing contact for burst usage reconciliation.

A few implementation items I want to flag so the onboarding work can be sequenced:
1) Network: we need VPC peering + a short list of CIDR allowlists to provision; we put a sample network-diagram.png in the attachments.
2) Autoscale: Redwood recommends a two-tier autoscale policy for reserved pools: baseline reserved capacity (committed GPUs) + controlled burst (spot-backed or on-demand) with a hard cap. We typically recommend prewarm of 10% of burst capacity 30 minutes before anticipated peaks.
3) Caching: if your application uses repeating prefixes we can enable KV/prefix caching for up to 60% token savings — this affects the capacity estimate in capacity-estimates-2028-07.zip.

Next steps: if you can confirm the QPS/latency targets and procurement contact by EOD Friday (2028-07-19) we'll lock the activation window and send an updated SOW and DocuSign link.

Attachments: skyline-mtap-v2.pdf, capacity-estimates-2028-07.zip, network-diagram.png

Cheers,
Diego Fernandez
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 16 Jul 2028 11:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MTAP draft + regional burst question

Thanks Diego — this looks good and aligned with what we discussed. Answers inline below: 

- Peak sustained QPS: baseline 300 qps sustained, expected peaks up to 450 qps for short windows (5–15 minutes) during batch jobs.
- Latency targets: p50 <= 80ms, p95 <= 240ms for 512-token prompts. If we see regressions beyond p95 300ms we need automated fallback to a smaller model.
- Regions: yes, us-west-2 primary. eu-west-1 for failover; we also want ap-southeast-1 for low-latency APAC testing (read-only for now).
- Procurement: procurement@skyline.ai (CC'd) — they'll need the SOW and a 60-day signature window. Billing: matthew.h@skyline.ai (not on this thread).

Notes on autoscale/burst: we prefer a controlled burst model where committed GPUs cover 60% of expected peak and burst fills the rest. Important: any burst utilization must be metered and visible in near real-time for our finance team. Can Redwood expose token-level billing or a pre-aggregated burst usage dashboard?

I'll review the MTAP with our infra team and follow up with specific CIDRs by Thursday. Priya, looping you in for procurement timeline.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of ML Platforms, Skyline Labs
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@skyline.ai>, Priya Menon <priya.m@skyline.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2028 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MTAP draft + regional burst question

Alex / Priya — appreciate the quick clarifications. A few operational recommendations from CS/Onboarding so we can remove ambiguity in the MTAP before procurement: 

- Billing visibility: we can provide a near-real-time dashboard showing token-by-model and burst vs reserved breakdown (we typically surface it in the Console and send daily CSV exports to billing@skyline.ai). We'll include a short sample CSV in the provisioning folder once CIDRs are in.

- Autoscale policy suggestion (practical defaults):
  * Reserved baseline: provision to cover 60% of expected peak (as Alex suggested).
  * Burst ceiling: allow up to 200% of baseline using on-demand/spot with a configurable hard cap.
  * Prewarm: prewarm 10% of burst 30–45 minutes before scheduled batch windows.
  * Degradation policy: if p95 latency > 350ms for more than 2 minutes, automatically route to a smaller model variant and trigger a paging alert to the on-call SRE.

- Regional cutover plan (minimal disruption):
  1) Provision us-west-2 reserved pool and test with sample traffic (week 0).
  2) Enable burst for us-west-2 with 30% prewarming for first week of live traffic.
  3) Stand up eu-west-1 as passive failover for week 2 and run failover drills.
  4) If ap-southeast-1 required later, we can enable read-only endpoints with lower capacity to validate latency.

Action items I captured for MTAP v2:
- Diego: update MTAP to include the autoscale thresholds above and add a short example CSV for billing exports.
- Alex: share CIDR blocks + a single billing contact email.
- Priya / Procurement: confirm DocuSign window (60 days ok?) and whether Skyline requests net-45 or net-30 terms.

I'll schedule a 30-minute runbook review next week (suggested slots: Tue 7/23 or Wed 7/24 at 10am PT).

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MTAP draft + regional burst question

Monica / Diego — thanks for the clear asklist. Procurement confirms: 60-day review window is fine; Skyline prefers net-30 payment terms. We'll need an itemized SOW + reserved capacity pricing and a separate schedule for burst rates before we route to legal. Can Redwood include a clause for a single 30-day SLA credit for regional outages > 4 hours? Our legal team will want to review SLA language but this helps speed approvals.

Also confirming: CIDRs will be sent by EOD Friday (2028-08-04) and billing contact is matthew.h@skyline.ai. Please send the updated MTAP and SOW to procurement@skyline.ai when ready — we'll aim to sign within the 60-day window contingent on final pricing.

On the operational side, one ask: can Redwood expose an alert webhook when burst utilization exceeds 70% of the configured burst ceiling? That would let our ops automate throttles for some non-critical workloads.

Next steps (agreed):
- Redwood (Diego/Monica): update MTAP with autoscale thresholds, prewarm schedule, sample billing CSV, and SOW with reserved + burst pricing.
- Skyline (Alex/Priya): send CIDRs, furnish billing contact, and confirm net-30.
- Procurement: expect DocuSign when SOW is finalized; legal to review SLA clause once included.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Menon
